scope.summary: struct-atomicity now resolves the changed struct to its defining crate-root module and only counts literal sites whose name resolves to that module, ending the rule-17 false positive where two unrelated private structs in different modules shared a name; genuine orphaned initializers are still refused and every ambiguous name fails closed.
out_of_scope: No type-aware analysis beyond module/import resolution: re-exports, macro-generated modules and items, and cross-crate aliasing are deliberately unresolved and therefore fail closed (site kept as a candidate).
No weakening of the refusal: a name that cannot be placed, a glob import, a re-export, or an unresolvable qualified path all keep the site as a candidate, so a real orphan still exits 65.
The existing --staged per-file touched rule is unchanged: an un-updated literal inside the same touched file is still not detected (pre-existing limitation, not addressed here).
Other dirty paths in the shared multi-agent checkout (crates/**, docs/ci_taxonomy.json, .beads/**, refactor/**, web/**) are other agents mid-edit and are excluded from this scope.

entry_points.name: bash scripts/swarm_discipline.sh struct-atomicity --staged / --commit HEAD (real repo)
entry_points.trace: Run 2026-09-28 from the repo root; both exit 0 with '0 added struct field(s); no orphaned initializer sites', confirming the new module-resolution precompute completes on the full workspace tree without error.

limitations: Verified on the local Linux multi-agent host only; no CI run on this SHA was observed, so readiness stays not-ready / scoped-test.

The module resolver recognises file modules (lib.rs/main.rs, foo.rs, foo/mod.rs and their nested layout) and module-scope inline `mod name { }` blocks; it does not parse macro-generated modules. A name it cannot place is treated as a candidate, so the miss cannot hide an orphan.

Re-exports (`pub use ...`) are not followed: if a use target module does not itself define the item, the site fails closed and stays a candidate. This can retain a false positive in a re-export layout, but never a false negative.
The pre-existing per-file touched rule still means an un-updated literal inside the same file that adds the field is not flagged; that behaviour is unchanged by this bead.

The negative acceptance case necessarily uses a crate-visible (pub(crate)) changed struct imported by an untouched module, because a private struct cannot be referenced from another module; the false-positive half of the pair remains two truly private same-named structs.
